title: Lockstep simulation during the first phase
statement: Let $M_1,M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $c$ be a configuration of $M_1$ on $x$, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that at every time $s<t$, the configuration reached by running $M_1$ from $c$ for $s$ steps is not halted. Then running the buffered composition from the first-phase embedding of $c$ for $t$ steps yields the first-phase embedding of the configuration reached by running $M_1$ from $c$ for $t$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1,M_2$ are finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
for every $s<t$, the run of $M_1$ from $c$ at time $s$ is not halted
replaced:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be machines over the Boolean alphabet with finitely many
states, let $c$ be a configuration of $M_1$ on input $x$, and let $t$ be a
number of steps such that the run of $M_1$ from $c$ has not halted at any
time strictly before $t$.  Then running the buffered sequential composition
of $M_1$ and $M_2$ for $t$ steps from the first-phase embedding of $c$ yields
the first-phase embedding of the run of $M_1$ for $t$ steps from $c$.  The
time $t$ itself may be the first halting time of $M_1$.
